name: Iolani Palace
unique: The only royal palace on American soil, with a throne room, a koa wood staircase and the quilt the queen made in prison, restored to the 1890s.
buzz: The audio tour is the way to see it and the basement galleries add the overthrow story; book ahead and wear the booties they give you.

name: Polynesian Cultural Center
unique: A living museum of six Polynesian cultures with villages, canoe pageants and a evening show, run by students from across the Pacific.
buzz: The evening show is the spectacle and the villages are the learning; it is expensive and the luau package is the full experience.

name: Koko Head Crater Trail
unique: A climb up 1,048 railroad ties on an old military tramway to a crater rim view of Hanauma Bay and the southeast coast.
buzz: The stairs are relentless and the view is the reward; go at sunrise, the trail is exposed and crowded later.

name: Maui Tropical Plantation
unique: A working farm with a tram tour through tropical crops, a duck pond and a restaurant that cooks what grows on the grounds.
buzz: The tram is good with children and the farm-to-table restaurant is the reason adults come back; the zip line is the add on.

name: Kauai Plantation Railway
unique: A narrow gauge train through a working plantation where you feed the pigs and pick fruit, ending at a 1930s plantation house.
buzz: Children love the animals and the ride and the rum tasting at the manor is for the adults; the train is short and the grounds are pretty.

name: Hanalei Bay
unique: A crescent bay backed by mountains and a pier, with a river mouth, a reef and a view of the Na Pali coast from the water.
buzz: The bay is the postcard of Kauai and the winter surf is for experts; parking is tight and the north shore gets rain.

name: Hilo Farmers Market
unique: An open air market with 200 vendors selling rambutan, apple bananas, poke and orchid stems, in a town that gets 130 inches of rain a year.
buzz: Go early for the fruit and the poke; the Wednesday and Saturday markets are the big ones and the prices are the best on the island.

name: Akaka Falls
unique: A 442 foot waterfall dropping into a gorge of bamboo and ferns, reached by a loop trail through a rain forest of orchids and ginger.
buzz: The falls are the photograph and the loop is paved with stairs; it rains often and the trail is slippery, which is why it is green.

name: Kalaupapa Trail
unique: A 1,700 foot cliff trail with 26 switchbacks down to the leprosy settlement where Father Damien served, now a national historical park.
buzz: The trail is steep and the settlement is still home to patients, so visits are guided and respectful; book through a licensed operator.

name: National Archives
unique: The rotunda holding the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution and the Bill of Rights in dim cases, with a mural of the founders above them.
buzz: The documents are faded and the room is dark and it still lands; go at opening to avoid the school groups.

name: Supreme Court
company: Supreme Court of the United States
unique: The marble temple with a courtroom you can sit in, a spiral staircase and exhibits on the cases that shaped the country.
buzz: The courtroom and the self guided tour are free and quick; oral argument days need a line and the building is across from the Capitol.

name: National Portrait Gallery
unique: Portraits of every president and the people who changed the country, including the Lansdowne portrait of Washington, in a former patent office building.
buzz: The presidential gallery and the modern portraits are the route and the courtyard is the quiet break; it is free and connected to the American Art Museum.

name: Phillips Collection
unique: The first museum of modern art in the country, in a Dupont Circle house with Renoirs, Rothkos and a Rothko room designed for quiet looking.
buzz: The Rothko room is the reason people return and the house scale makes it intimate; it is small and the admission is modest.

name: Frederick Douglass National Historic Site
unique: Cedar Hill, the house Douglass bought after the war, with his library, his desk and a view over the Anacostia and the Capitol.
buzz: The ranger tour is the only way in and the view from the porch is half the story; the site is in a neighborhood most visitors never see.

name: Union Market
unique: A 1931 wholesale market turned food hall with butchers, a tortilleria, a oyster counter and a rotating set of pop ups, north of Capitol Hill.
buzz: The food stalls change often and the oyster bar and the tacos are the standards; it is busy on weekends and easier on weekdays.

name: Nationals Park
unique: A ballpark on the Anacostia with a center field plaza, a presidents race in the fourth inning and a view of the Capitol from the upper deck.
buzz: The presidents race is the tradition and the standing room areas are good; tickets are cheap on weeknights and the metro stops at the gate.

name: National Museum of the American Indian
unique: A curvilinear limestone building on the Mall with a collection organized by tribe rather than chronology, and a cafeteria of Native dishes from across the hemisphere.
buzz: The cafeteria is a destination on its own and the galleries reward slow reading; the building's form and the landscape design are part of the exhibit.

name: Hillwood Estate
unique: The estate of the Post cereal heiress, with a collection of Russian imperial art including Faberge eggs, and a Japanese garden and French parterre.
buzz: The Faberge collection is the reason art people come and the gardens are the quiet afternoon; it is off the tourist track and never crowded.

name: Tidal Basin Paddle Boats
company: DC Department of Parks and Recreation
unique: A paddle boat on the Tidal Basin with the Jefferson Memorial on one side and the cherry trees on the other, from the water.
buzz: The view from the water is different from the shore and the boats are cheap; the basin is shallow and the queue is long in cherry blossom week.

name: Marble House
customer: House tour people, architecture fans, families
unique: A Vanderbilt summer cottage of 500,000 cubic feet of marble, with a gold ballroom and a Chinese tea house on the cliff walk.
buzz: The ballroom and the tea house are the stops and the audio tour explains the suffrage history of the owner; the cliff walk access is the bonus.

name: Colt State Park
unique: A 464 acre shore park on Narragansett Bay with a bike loop, formal gardens, a beach and a view of the Providence skyline.
buzz: The bike loop and the shore road are the local ritual and the park is free; the breeze keeps it cool in summer.

name: Wilcox Park
unique: An Olmsted designed park with a pond, specimen trees and the Shakespeare library at its edge, in a town of 22,000.
buzz: The park and the library are the quiet afternoon and the summer concerts on the green are the local tradition; it is free.

name: Point Judith
unique: The rocky point where Narragansett Bay meets Block Island Sound, with a lighthouse, a surf beach and a row of clam shacks.
buzz: The clam cakes and the view of the lighthouse are the stop and the surf is consistent; the point is windy and the rocks are slippery.

name: Museum of Work and Culture
unique: A museum in a former textile mill telling the story of the French Canadian workers who came to the mills, with a mill floor and a company store.
buzz: The mill floor and the immigration story are the reasons to come; it is specific and local and the guides know the families.

name: Idaho Anne Frank Human Rights Memorial
unique: An outdoor memorial along the Boise River with a bronze of Anne Frank at her diary, quotations carved in stone and a replica of the attic wall.
buzz: It is quiet and free and the quotations are the reason people stop; the greenbelt trail runs past it for a longer walk.

name: Basque Block
unique: A downtown block of Basque restaurants, a market and a cultural center, in the city with the largest Basque community outside Spain.
buzz: The family style dinners and the market's chorizo are the reasons to come and the July Jaialdi festival fills the city; the block is small.

name: Idaho Falls Greenbelt
unique: A five mile paved path along the Snake River past a 20 foot waterfall in the middle of town, with a Japanese garden and a museum.
buzz: The falls in the center of town are the surprise and the path is flat; the greenbelt connects the zoo, the art museum and the river.

name: Bear Lake
unique: A 20 mile lake on the Utah border with turquoise water, a state park beach and raspberry shakes sold in the town of Garden City.
buzz: The water is clear and the color is the reason people drive; the lake is cold in June and the shakes are the tradition.

name: Lake Pend Oreille
unique: One of the deepest lakes in the country, 43 miles long below the Selkirk Mountains, with a town beach, a ski hill and Navy acoustic testing.
buzz: The lake and the mountains are the reason people move to Sandpoint and the summer water is cold; the winter ski hill is right above town.

name: Sierra Silver Mine Tour
unique: A trolley ride and a walk into a real silver mine tunnel under Wallace, with a retired miner explaining the drills and the ore cars.
buzz: The guides are miners and the tunnel is cool; Wallace itself is a silver town with a historic district worth an hour.
